title: Semi-Final Preview: Argentina vs France in World Cup 2026 Blockbuster
summary: Argentina and France meet again in a World Cup semi-final, reprising their epic 2022 final in what promises to be the match of the tournament.
content:
Football's two most compelling narratives converge at MetLife Stadium as Argentina and France contest a World Cup semi-final that carries echoes of their unforgettable 2022 final in Lusail. The anticipation surrounding this fixture has been building since the draw, and both sides have navigated their paths to this stage with authority and flair.

Argentina's Title Defence

Lionel Scaloni's Argentina have been the model of consistency throughout the tournament, winning five matches from five with a blend of tactical discipline and individual brilliance. Lionel Messi, at 38, continues to defy the passage of time with three assists and one goal, his vision and passing range still unmatched in world football. Julian Alvarez has shouldered the goalscoring burden magnificently with four goals, while Enzo Fernandez has cemented his status as the world's premier box-to-box midfielder with a series of commanding performances.

France's Firepower

Didier Deschamps' France have been the tournament's most devastating attacking force, scoring 14 goals in five matches. Kylian Mbappe leads the Golden Boot race with six goals and has been virtually unplayable, his combination of pace, power, and finishing making him the most feared striker on the planet. Behind him, Antoine Griezmann continues to orchestrate play with his customary intelligence, while Aurelien Tchouameni provides the defensive steel that allows France's attackers to flourish.

The Tactical Chessboard

The key battle will be in midfield, where Fernandez and Rodrigo De Paul must contain the supply line to Mbappe. Argentina's preference for controlling possession will be tested by France's willingness to concede territory and strike on the counter-attack at devastating speed. The wide areas will be critical, with Nahuel Molina and Nicolas Tagliafico needing to balance their attacking instincts against the threat of Ousmane Dembele and Mbappe in transition.

What the Managers Say

Scaloni has spoken of the mutual respect between the two squads, while Deschamps has emphasized that revenge for the 2022 final is not a motivating factor. Both managers know that fine margins will decide this encounter. Set pieces, substitutions, and the ability to handle pressure in the closing stages could all prove decisive in what promises to be a contest worthy of a World Cup final.
